newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan currency surges after Taleban takeover.
newsitem.headline: Afghan currency surges after Taleban takeover.

text.p: Afghanistan's currency, the afghani, surged to 11,000 to the U.S. dollar on Friday from the 18,500 level it was trading at before Taleban Islamic militia captured the capital Kabul, currency dealers said.
"We think the afghani will strengthen when the market reopens tommorrow," Javaid, a money changer near the Pul-i-Khishti mosque, told Reuters.

"Fighting is over and there will be no need to pay officials and mujahideens to fight this or that faction and the roads will be opened," Javaid said. "There will be no checkpoints on the roads to extort money."
Money changers in the Afghan capital's currency exchange market said that rumours that former King Zahir Shah might return to Kabul had also pushed the afghani up against the dollar.

The afghani had sunk to more than 20,000 to the dollar in recent weeks, driving prices of food and fuel out of reach of the ordinary people in Kabul, where government servants make the equivalent of $3 a month in salary.
